Order the findings by severity: contradictions that could cause data loss or a broken deploy first, then missing entries, then duplicates.

78	## Key learnings & principles
79	
80	- Docker Compose env vars override `app.ini` on every restart — never hand-edit config files for settings also declared as env vars; the compose file is authoritative
81	- Image tag staleness: `ghcr.io/usememos/memos:latest` was silently pinned at an old version despite repeated pulls; switching registries (`neosmemo/memos:stable`) resolved it — always verify actual running version
82	- Backup verification is not optional: Forgejo backups appeared configured but produced 0-byte SQLite snapshots silently for months
83	- SQLite in WAL mode has a second route to the same disaster: the main `.db` can sit at 4 KB with every row still in the `-wal`, so an rsync of the `.db` alone captures a database with *no rows* — and it opens cleanly and reports `integrity_check: ok`. Always `sqlite3 .backup` (checkpoints first); on restore always delete stale `-wal`/`-shm` first, or SQLite replays the old WAL over the file you just restored and silently reverts it. A clean container stop is what removes those files, which is why `init: true` matters for any PID-1 Node process
84	- A health endpoint that only reads proves almost nothing: SQLite answers reads from its page cache with the database file deleted, and a full disk only affects writes. Probe with a real write if the check is meant to page you
85	- `occ dav:delete-calendar` without `--force` only trashes calendars; `dav:list-calendars` keeps showing tombstoned rows, causing duplicate-suffixed calendar accumulation

87	- DNS bypass vectors for filtering: browser built-in secure DNS, iOS Private Relay, VPN apps, cellular connections — never list a public resolver as secondary DHCP DNS
88	- Nextcloud/WebDAV sync reliability: chunked uploads (`max_chunk_size`), `bulkupload.enabled => false`, `filesystem_check_changes => 1` improve stability over plain WebDAV

270	### CalDAV discovery (July 26, 2026)
271	
272	The `.well-known/caldav` and `.well-known/carddav` redirects are handled by
273	**Caddy**, not by Nextcloud. Without this, the redirect is generated by
274	Apache inside `nextcloud-app-1`, which sees a plain-HTTP connection behind
275	the proxy and therefore emits an absolute `http://` Location. CalDAV clients
276	that follow it fail at the discovery step — Homarr reported
277	`cannot find principalUrl`.
278	
279	Note that the `overwrite*` settings do **not** fix this. They govern URLs
280	generated by PHP; this redirect is emitted by Apache before PHP runs, and
281	Apache does not consult Nextcloud's config. The `overwrite*` and
282	`trusted_proxies` values were already correct when this was diagnosed.
283	
284	Verify with:
285	
286	```bash
287	curl -sI https://celen.cloud/.well-known/caldav | head -5
288	```
289	
290	Expect `location: https://celen.cloud/remote.php/dav/` and `server: Caddy`.
291	A `content-type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1` means Apache answered and the
292	Caddy `redir` lines are missing.

938	Unlike most services here this is not a registry image — it builds locally
939	from the repo via a multi-stage `node:24-alpine` Dockerfile. `better-sqlite3`
940	resolves to its bundled `linuxmusl-x64` prebuild, so nothing compiles from
941	source and a clean build is ~40s.
942	
943	### Auth
944	
945	Two bearer tokens in `~/onetab-next/.env` (mode `600`), both in Vaultwarden:
946	
947	- `API_TOKEN` — full read/write/delete. Used by the extension and the web UI.
948	- `API_TOKEN_READONLY` — GET-only. This is the one for the Homarr widget, so
949	  a leaked dashboard config can't delete anything.
950	
951	The server refuses to start if `API_TOKEN` is missing, still the
952	`.env.example` placeholder, or under 24 characters.
953	
954	### Container hardening
955	
956	`read_only: true` rootfs with `tmpfs: /tmp`, `cap_drop: ALL`,
957	`no-new-privileges`, non-root fixed UID/GID `10001`, port published only on
958	loopback, `json-file` logging capped at 10 MB × 3.
959	
960	`init: true` is **load-bearing, not decoration**. Node runs as PID 1, and a
961	PID-1 process with the default signal disposition ignores `SIGTERM` — without
962	an init, `docker compose down` would wait out the full stop grace period and
963	then `SIGKILL`, giving the app no chance to close the database. See the
964	backup note below for why that matters here specifically.
965	
966	### Health endpoint
967	
968	`GET /api/health`, unauthenticated (so Uptime Kuma and the Docker healthcheck
969	can reach it). It is deliberately **not** a static `{ok: true}`: it stats the
970	database file, compares its inode against the one open at startup, and
971	performs a small write to a single-row `health_probe` table. A read-only
972	probe cannot detect a full disk, a read-only mount, or a database replaced
973	underneath the process — SQLite serves reads from its page cache and keeps
974	writing happily to an unlinked inode. The probe result is cached 5 s so the
975	endpoint can't be used to amplify writes.
976	
977	Known limit: it cannot detect a database replaced **in place** by `cp`, which
978	truncates and rewrites through the same inode. That is exactly why the
979	restore procedure below stops the container first.
980	
981	### Favicons
982	
983	Proxied server-side rather than loaded from the source site, so the dashboard
984	doesn't leak its IP, timing and referrer to every site in the saved history.
985	The proxy accepts only real image content types — `image/x` and
986	`image/x"><script>` were admitted by an earlier `image/` prefix test and are
987	not now — and connects only to ports 80/443, which stops a token holder using
988	it as an authenticated port scanner.
989	
990	`image/svg+xml` **is** accepted, deliberately. Excluding it (as a security
991	pass once suggested) blanked the icon for every site that ships an SVG
992	favicon, which is a real regression traded for a theoretical gain: the
993	dashboard only ever paints these bytes into an `<img>`, where no script runs
994	whatever the type. It's neutralised at the response instead — every favicon
995	is served `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; sandbox` plus
996	`Content-Disposition: inline`, so an SVG carrying `<script>` is inert even on
997	direct navigation.

999	### Homarr integration
1000	
1001	An **iFrame widget** pointed at the purpose-built embed view:
1002	
1003	```
1004	https://tabs.celen.cloud/embed#token=<API_TOKEN_READONLY>&limit=8
1005	```
1006	
1007	It renders a count summary and the most recent groups; clicking a group
1008	expands it in place to list its tabs, and each tab links to its own URL.
1009	Nothing in the tile links back to the dashboard — `/` sends
1010	`frame-ancestors 'none'`, so navigating the frame there produces
1011	`ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE` inside the tile. Outbound links go through an
1012	explicit `window.open`, because a bare `target="_blank"` is dropped when the
1013	embedder sandboxes its iframe without `allow-popups` and can degrade into
1014	exactly that in-frame navigation. The token goes in the URL **fragment**, not
1015	the query string, so it never reaches the server, never
1016	lands in Caddy's access log, and is not sent in `Referer`. Use the read-only
1017	token — a widget config is a plausible leak point.
1018	
1019	Framing is refused unless `EMBED_ALLOWED_ANCESTOR` in `~/onetab-next/.env`
1020	names the Homarr origin exactly (`https://bogac.celen.cloud`, no trailing
1021	slash). `/embed` is the only framable page on this host; the main dashboard
1022	holds a full-access token in `localStorage` and stays `frame-ancestors 'none'`
1023	regardless. `/embed` is also served `Cache-Control: no-store`, because its CSP
1024	is derived from that env var — a response cached before the variable was set
1025	keeps enforcing the old policy and the browser goes on refusing to frame a
1026	page the server now allows. That cost an hour of debugging on first setup:
1027	the headers were correct on the wire while Chrome kept using a stale copy.
1028	
1029	Note that editing `.env` alone is not enough — `docker compose restart` does
1030	not re-read `env_file`, so a change needs `docker compose up -d`.

1032	An app tile (plain link) and a Custom API widget against

1149	  the variable only in `sudo`'s environment, not the invoking shell, so the
1150	  expansion happens against an empty value.
